source.text: וַיֵּ֥רַע אֶל־יוֹנָ֖ה רָעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיִּ֖חַר לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was evil to Jonah, an evil great, and it burned to him.

en.L: But it was evil to Jonah, a great evil, and he became hot [with anger].
en.B: But to Jonah this seemed a great wrong, and he became angry.
en.R: But Jonah was very upset about this, and he became angry.

vi.L: Nhưng điều ấy là điều ác đối với Giô-na, một điều ác lớn, và ông nổi nóng.
vi.B: Nhưng Giô-na thấy việc ấy là một điều rất sai trái, và ông nổi giận.
vi.R: Nhưng Giô-na rất bực bội về việc này, và ông nổi giận.

es.L: Pero [esto] le pareció mal a Jonás, un gran mal, y se encendió [en ira].
es.B: Pero a Jonás esto le pareció una gran injusticia, y se enojó.
es.R: Pero Jonás se disgustó mucho por esto, y se enojó.

fr.L: Mais ce fut un mal pour Jonas, un grand mal, et il s’enflamma [de colère].
fr.B: Mais Jonas trouva cela profondément mauvais, et il se mit en colère.
fr.R: Mais Jonas a été très contrarié, et il s’est mis en colère.

sw.L: Lakini jambo hilo likawa ubaya kwa Yona, ubaya mkubwa, naye akawaka [hasira].
sw.B: Lakini Yona aliona jambo hilo kuwa baya sana, akakasirika.
sw.R: Lakini jambo hilo lilimchukiza Yona sana, akakasirika.

ko.L: 그러나 이 일이 요나에게 악했으니, 큰 악이었다. 그래서 그가 [분노로] 달아올랐다.
ko.B: 그러나 요나에게는 이 일이 크게 잘못된 일로 보였다. 그래서 그는 화가 났다.
ko.R: 그러나 요나는 이 일 때문에 몹시 언짢았다. 그래서 그는 화를 냈다.

pt.L: Mas [isso] foi mal para Jonas, um grande mal, e ele se inflamou [de ira].
pt.B: Mas, para Jonas, isso foi um grande mal, e ele ficou irado.
pt.R: Mas isso deixou Jonas muito aborrecido, e ele ficou com raiva.

decisions.choice: it was evil to Jonah, a great evil: Jonah was deeply displeased
decisions.reason: The book's word for evil and disaster (see 1:2) comes back with the word "great". Nineveh turned from evil and God turned from disaster; now Jonah thinks it evil, a great one, that God has done so. The verse turns the words of the story against him.

decisions.choice: it burned to him: he became angry
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, anger "burns". The same verb comes in the LORD's question, "Is it good that it burns to you?" (4:4, 9).

decisions.choice: a great evil (L); a great wrong (B); very upset (R); hot [with anger] (L); angry (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "evil" and "great", so the reader can see both words return. Balanced says "a great wrong"; Readable says how Jonah felt.

decisions.choice: "le pareció mal ..., un gran mal" (L); "se encendió [en ira]" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the book's word "mal" and the Hebrew picture of anger as burning; Balanced and Readable use "se enojó".

decisions.choice: "akawaka [hasira]"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "it burned to him"; Swahili "kuwaka hasira" is the natural idiom, and Literal brackets "hasira" as the English brackets "[with anger]". The same in 4:4 and 4:9.

decisions.choice: "악했으니, 큰 악이었다" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the book's word "evil" (meaning decision): what was evil for Nineveh in 3:10 is now "evil" to Jonah. Balanced and Readable say he was deeply displeased.

decisions.choice: "điều ác ... một điều ác lớn" (L); "một điều rất sai trái" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the book's word "evil", now turned on what God has done; Balanced says how it seemed to Jonah, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "ce fut un mal pour Jonas, un grand mal" (L); "Jonas trouva cela profondément mauvais" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the book's word for evil ("mal", "mauvais"), which the English meaning decision follows through the story.

source.text: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל אֶל־יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּאמַ֗ר אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ הֲלוֹא־זֶ֣ה דְבָרִ֗י עַד־הֱיוֹתִי֙ עַל־אַדְמָתִ֔י עַל־כֵּ֥ן קִדַּ֖מְתִּי לִבְרֹ֣חַ תַּרְשִׁ֑ישָׁה כִּ֣י יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ אֵֽל־חַנּ֣וּן וְרַח֔וּם אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֨יִם֙ וְרַב־חֶ֔סֶד וְנִחָ֖ם עַל־הָרָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he prayed to Yahweh and said, Please, Yahweh, [was] not this my word while I was on my land? Therefore I acted first to flee to Tarshish; for I knew that you [are] a God gracious and compassionate, long of anger and great of loyal love, and relenting concerning the evil.

en.L: And he prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [was] this not my word while I was still in my own land? That is why I acted first to flee to Tarshish; for I knew that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] a God gracious and compassionate, long of anger, and great in steadfast love, and relenting concerning the evil.
en.B: He prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, did I not say this while I was still in my own country? That is why I hurried to run away to Tarshish. For I knew that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a God of grace and tender compassion, slow to grow angry, rich in faithful love, and one who relents from sending disaster.
en.R: Jonah prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I said this would happen when I was still at home! That is why I hurried to run away to Tarshish. I knew that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a God of kindness and tender mercy. You are slow to become angry. Your faithful love is great. You change {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mind about punishing people.

vi.L: Ông cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và nói: "Ôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, chẳng phải đây là lời con [đã nói] khi con còn ở quê hương con sao? Vì thế con đã vội trốn đến Ta-rê-si trước; vì con biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] Đức Chúa Trời ban ơn và đầy lòng thương xót, chậm giận, và dồi dào tình yêu thương thành tín, và đổi ý về tai họa.
vi.B: Ông cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Ôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, chẳng phải con đã nói điều này khi con còn ở quê nhà sao? Vì thế con đã vội vàng chạy trốn đến Ta-rê-si. Vì con biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Đức Chúa Trời đầy ân điển và lòng trắc ẩn, chậm nóng giận, giàu tình yêu thương thành tín, và đổi ý không giáng tai họa.
vi.R: Giô-na cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Ôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, khi con còn ở quê nhà, con đã nói việc này sẽ xảy ra mà! Vì thế con đã vội chạy trốn đến Ta-rê-si. Con biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Đức Chúa Trời nhân từ và đầy lòng thương xót. Ngài chậm giận. Tình thương thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật lớn lao. Ngài đổi ý, không trừng phạt người ta.

es.L: Y oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijo: «Te ruego, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿no [era] esta mi palabra cuando aún estaba yo en mi tierra? Por eso me adelanté a huir a Tarsis; porque yo sabía que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} [eres] un Dios benévolo y compasivo, lento para la ira y grande en amor leal, y que se retracta del mal.
es.B: Oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Por favor, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿no dije esto cuando todavía estaba en mi país? Por eso me apresuré a huir a Tarsis. Porque yo sabía que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres un Dios de gracia y de compasión entrañable, lento para enojarse, rico en amor fiel, y que desiste de enviar el desastre.
es.R: Jonás oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Por favor, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡yo dije que esto iba a pasar cuando todavía estaba en casa! Por eso me apresuré a huir a Tarsis. Yo sabía que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres un Dios lleno de bondad y de ternura. No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} enojas fácilmente. Tu amor fiel es grande. Estás dispuesto a cambiar de parecer y no enviar el castigo.

fr.L: Et il pria {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et dit : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, n’[était]-ce pas là ma parole quand j’étais encore dans mon pays ? C’est pourquoi j’ai pris les devants en fuyant à Tarsis ; car je savais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} [es] un Dieu favorable et compatissant, lent à la colère, et grand en amour fidèle, et qui renonce au mal.
fr.B: Il pria {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, n’est-ce pas ce que je disais quand j’étais encore dans mon pays ? C’est pour cela que je me suis empressé de m’enfuir à Tarsis. Car je savais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es un Dieu plein de grâce et de tendre compassion, lent à se mettre en colère, riche en amour fidèle, et qui renonce à envoyer le malheur.
fr.R: Jonas a prié {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je savais bien que cela arriverait, quand j’étais encore chez moi ! C’est pour cela que je me suis dépêché de m’enfuir à Tarsis. Je savais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es un Dieu plein de bonté et de tendresse. Tu ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} mets pas vite en colère. Ton amour fidèle est grand. Tu renonces à punir les gens.

sw.L: Akamwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali, je, hili halikuwa neno langu nilipokuwa bado katika nchi yangu? Ndiyo sababu nilitangulia kukimbilia Tarshishi; kwa maana nilijua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} [ni] Mungu wa neema na wa huruma, mkawivu wa hasira, na mwingi wa upendo usiokoma, unayeghairi kuhusu ubaya.
sw.B: Akamwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali, je, sikusema hivi nilipokuwa bado katika nchi yangu? Ndiyo sababu niliharakisha kukimbilia Tarshishi. Kwa maana nilijua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mungu mwingi wa neema na mwenye huruma ya moyoni, anayechelewa kukasirika, aliyejaa upendo usiokoma, na anayeghairi kuleta maafa.
sw.R: Yona akamwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali! Nilisema kwamba hili lingetokea nilipokuwa bado nyumbani! Ndiyo sababu niliharakisha kukimbilia Tarshishi. Nilijua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mungu mwenye wema na huruma tele. Hukasiriki upesi. Upendo {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} usiokoma ni mkubwa. Unabadili nia {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na kuacha kuwaadhibu watu.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도하여 말했다. "아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 아직 제 땅에 있을 때에 이것이 제 말이 아니었습니까? 그래서 제가 먼저 다시스로 도망하려 했던 것입니다. 주님은 은혜롭고 긍휼이 많은 하나님이시며, 분노를 오래 참으시고 한결같은 사랑이 크시며, 재앙에 대하여 뜻을 돌이키시는 분이심을 제가 알았기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 고향에 있을 때에 이미 이렇게 말하지 않았습니까? 그래서 제가 서둘러 다시스로 달아나려 했던 것입니다. 주님은 은혜를 베푸시고 불쌍히 여기시는 하나님이시며, 쉽게 노하지 않으시고 한결같은 사랑이 넘치시며, 재앙을 내리시려다가도 뜻을 돌이키시는 분이라는 것을 제가 알고 있었습니다.
ko.R: 요나가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 고향에 있을 때에 이렇게 될 거라고 말씀드리지 않았습니까! 그래서 제가 서둘러 다시스로 달아나려고 했던 것입니다. 저는 주님이 친절을 베푸시고 따뜻한 사랑으로 불쌍히 여기시는 하나님이신 줄 알았습니다. 주님은 좀처럼 화를 내지 않으십니다. 주님의 변함없는 사랑은 큽니다. 주님은 마음을 바꾸셔서 사람들에게 벌을 내리지 않으십니다.

pt.L: E ele orou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e disse: "Por favor, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, não [era] esta a minha palavra quando eu ainda estava na minha terra? Por isso me antecipei fugindo para Társis; pois eu sabia que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} [és] um Deus misericordioso e compassivo, longo de ira e grande em amor leal, e que desiste do mal.
pt.B: Ele orou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Por favor, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, não foi isso que eu disse quando ainda estava na minha terra? Foi por isso que me apressei a fugir para Társis. Pois eu sabia que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és um Deus misericordioso e compassivo, lento para se irar e cheio de amor leal, e que desiste de mandar a desgraça.
pt.R: Jonas orou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Por favor, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, eu disse que isso ia acontecer quando ainda estava em casa! Foi por isso que fugi depressa para Társis. Eu sabia que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és um Deus bondoso e cheio de compaixão. Tu demoras a ficar irado. O {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} amor fiel é grande. Tu estás sempre pronto a mudar de ideia e não mandar a desgraça.

decisions.choice: a God gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, great in loyal love: the words of Exodus 34:6
decisions.reason: When the LORD passed before Moses he proclaimed himself "a God compassionate and gracious, long of anger, and great in steadfast love and faithfulness" (Exodus 34:6). Jonah quotes it with the first two words in the other order, as Joel 2:13 and Psalm 145:8 have them, leaves out "and faithfulness", and adds "relenting concerning the evil", as Joel 2:13 does. Israel praised God in these words (Psalm 86:15; 103:8; Nehemiah 9:17); Jonah uses them as a complaint.

decisions.choice: relenting concerning the evil: turning back from the disaster he has threatened
decisions.reason: This is the verb of 3:9-10, used with the book's word for evil and disaster (see 1:2). Jonah has seen God do exactly this for Nineveh.

decisions.choice: was this not my word? Jonah gives the reason he fled
decisions.reason: Only now does the reader learn why Jonah ran away in chapter 1: not from fear, but because he knew God would forgive Nineveh, and he did not want that. The book does not say what lay behind it. Nineveh was the capital of Assyria, Israel's great enemy, and Jonah's anger may be that of a man who wanted justice on the city instead of mercy.

decisions.choice: I acted first: I tried to forestall it
decisions.reason: The verb means to go before, to act ahead of time. Jonah ran to Tarshish to get ahead of what he knew God would do, so as not to be the one who brought Nineveh its warning.

decisions.choice: the words of Exodus 34:6 at each level, with "gracious" and "compassionate" in Jonah's order; steadfast love (L); faithful love (B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its wording of Exodus 34:6, as set for Jonah 4:2: "long of anger" and "great in steadfast love" at Literal, "slow to grow angry, rich in faithful love" at Balanced, "slow to become angry" and "faithful love is great" at Readable. For that reason *hesed* here is "steadfast love" at Literal, as in Exodus, not "loyal love" as elsewhere in the prophets. Readable addresses God as "you" throughout and says "change your mind about punishing people" for relenting from disaster.

decisions.choice: Please, LORD (all levels); I said this would happen (R)
decisions.reason: "Please, LORD" is the same cry the sailors used (1:14), and every level keeps it. Readable turns the question "was this not my word?" into the statement it implies. Jonah's prayer is in prose, as the chapter is, and his words run to the end of verse 3.

decisions.choice: The published words of Exodus 34:6 at each level ("mkawivu wa hasira, na mwingi wa upendo usiokoma" L; "anayechelewa kukasirika, aliyejaa upendo usiokoma" B; "Hukasiriki upesi. Upendo wako usiokoma ni mkubwa" R), with "neema" and "huruma" in Jonah's order
decisions.reason: Jonah quotes the LORD's self-description (term sheet: Jonah 4:2 reuses Exodus 34:6). Exodus puts compassion before grace; Jonah reverses them, and Swahili follows Jonah. The Swahili Exodus already has "upendo usiokoma", so the English open question about hesed in this verse does not arise.

decisions.choice: The phrases of the Korean Exodus 34:6 at each level ("긍휼이 많고 은혜로운", "분노를 오래 참고", "한결같은 사랑" L; "불쌍히 여기며 은혜를 베푸는", "쉽게 노하지 않으며" B; "따뜻한 사랑으로 불쌍히 여기고 친절을 베푸는", "좀처럼 화를 내지 않는", "변함없는 사랑" R), in Jonah's order and with -시- because Jonah speaks to God
decisions.reason: The term sheet asks the Exodus 34:6 echoes to reuse the published Korean so the quotation is visible (meaning decision), as the Korean Joel 2:13 does. The English Literal says "steadfast love" here and "loyal love" in Joel; Korean has "한결같은 사랑" for both, so the founder's open English question does not change the Korean.

decisions.choice: Jonah keeps 합쇼체 to God even in his anger (4:2-3, 9)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: a prophet speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "저"; the anger is carried by the words, not by dropping the speech level.

decisions.choice: the published Exodus 34:6 at each level, with "ban ơn" and "thương xót" in Jonah's order ("ban ơn và đầy lòng thương xót, chậm giận, và dồi dào tình yêu thương thành tín", L)
decisions.reason: The terms note: Exodus 34:6 echoes reuse the published Vietnamese at each level. Jonah puts "gracious" before "compassionate", the reverse of Exodus, and the word order follows him. Vietnamese Exodus 34:6 already has "tình yêu thương thành tín" for hesed at L and B, so the English open question about "steadfast love" does not arise.

decisions.choice: Jonah says "Ôi, lạy CHÚA" and calls himself "con"
decisions.reason: The terms note: "Please, LORD" is "Ôi, lạy CHÚA", and a prophet says "con" to God. Compare 2:3, where the psalm keeps the Psalms' "tôi".

decisions.choice: "un Dios benévolo y compasivo, lento para la ira y grande en amor leal" (L); "un Dios de gracia y de compasión entrañable, lento para enojarse, rico en amor fiel" (B); "lleno de bondad y de ternura ... No te enojas fácilmente. Tu amor fiel es grande" (R)
decisions.reason: Jonah quotes Exodus 34:6, so each level reuses the published Spanish of that verse in Jonah's order ("gracious" before "compassionate"), with "amor leal" at Literal and "amor fiel" at Balanced and Readable, as Exodus 34:6 has them. Joel 2:13 and Micah 7:18-20 do the same: every quotation of Exodus 34:6-7 takes Exodus' wording.

decisions.choice: "se retracta del mal" (L); "desiste de enviar el desastre" (B); "Estás dispuesto a cambiar de parecer" (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Joel 2:13 in Spanish, which ends the same confession.

decisions.choice: The published Exodus 34:6 at each level ("compatissant et favorable, lent à la colère, grand en amour fidèle" L; "plein de tendre compassion et de grâce, lent à se mettre en colère, riche en amour fidèle" B; "plein de tendresse et de bonté ... ne se met pas vite en colère ... amour fidèle est grand" R), with "favorable" / "grâce" / "bonté" first, in Jonah's order
alternatives: "amour loyal" at Literal, as the prophets
decisions.reason: Jonah quotes Exodus 34:6; the term sheet has Jonah reuse Exodus's "amour fidèle" at Literal until the founder settles the ḥesed question.

decisions.choice: "qui renonce au mal" (L), "qui renonce à envoyer le malheur" (B), "Tu renonces à punir les gens" (R)
decisions.reason: As 3:9-10: God relenting is "renoncer à", never "se repentir".

decisions.choice: the Portuguese of Exodus 34:6 and Joel 2:13, in Jonah's order
decisions.reason: Jonah quotes Exodus 34:6 with "gracious" first (m1), as Joel 2:13 does, so each level uses Joel 2:13's Portuguese of the confession, spoken to God with "tu": "misericordioso e compassivo, longo de ira e grande em amor leal" (L), "misericordioso e compassivo, lento para se irar e cheio de amor leal" (B), "bondoso e cheio de compaixão ... demora a ficar irado ... amor fiel é grande" (R).

decisions.choice: desiste do mal (L); desiste de mandar a desgraça (B); pronto a mudar de ideia e não mandar a desgraça (R)
decisions.reason: Relenting is "desistir" at Literal and Balanced and "mudar de ideia" at Readable, as in 3:9-10 (m2); Balanced and Readable keep Joel 2:13's words for it. Literal says "do mal", the book's one word for evil and disaster (1:2), where Joel's Literal says "volta atrás quanto à desgraça".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה קַח־נָ֥א אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֛י ט֥וֹב מוֹתִ֖י מֵחַיָּֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And now, Yahweh, take, please, my life from me, for better [is] my death than my life.

en.L: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, take my life from me, please, for my death [is] better than my life."
en.B: So now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please take my life from me, for death is better for me than life."
en.R: So now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please let me die. I would rather be dead than alive."

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin lấy mạng sống con khỏi con, vì con chết còn hơn sống."
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin lấy mạng sống con đi, vì đối với con, chết còn hơn sống."
vi.R: Vậy bây giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin để con chết đi. Con thà chết còn hơn sống."

es.L: Y ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, quítame la vida, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ruego, porque mejor [es] mi muerte que mi vida».
es.B: Así que ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, por favor, quítame la vida, porque para mí es mejor la muerte que la vida».
es.R: Así que ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, por favor, déjame morir. Prefiero estar muerto que vivo».

fr.L: Et maintenant, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, prends donc ma vie loin de moi, car ma mort [est] meilleure que ma vie. »
fr.B: Maintenant donc, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, prends ma vie, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, car la mort vaut mieux pour moi que la vie. »
fr.R: Alors maintenant, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, laisse-moi mourir, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît. J’aime mieux être mort que vivant. »

sw.L: Basi sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali uchukue uhai wangu kutoka kwangu, kwa maana kufa kwangu [ni] bora kuliko kuishi kwangu."
sw.B: Basi sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali chukua uhai wangu, kwa maana ni afadhali nife kuliko kuishi."
sw.R: Basi sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali niache nife. Ni afadhali nife kuliko kuwa hai."

ko.L: 그러니 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제발 제 목숨을 제게서 거두어 주십시오. 제게는 죽는 것이 사는 것보다 낫기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 그러니 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제발 제 목숨을 거두어 주십시오. 저에게는 죽는 것이 사는 것보다 낫습니다."
ko.R: 그러니 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제발 저를 죽게 해 주십시오. 저는 사느니 차라리 죽는 것이 낫겠습니다."

pt.L: E agora, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, toma, por favor, a minha vida de mim, pois a minha morte [é] melhor do que a minha vida."
pt.B: Agora, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, por favor, tira a minha vida, pois para mim a morte é melhor do que a vida."
pt.R: Agora, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, por favor, deixa-me morrer. Prefiro estar morto a estar vivo."

decisions.choice: take my life: Elijah's prayer in 1 Kings 19:4
decisions.reason: Elijah, fleeing from Jezebel, sat under a broom tree and said, "Now, LORD, take my life, for I am not better than my fathers" (1 Kings 19:4). Jonah prays the same words, but Elijah was in despair because his work seemed to fail; Jonah is angry because his work has succeeded. 4:8 echoes the same verse again.

decisions.choice: take my life (L, B); let me die (R); death is better for me than life (B); rather be dead than alive (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "take my life", as in 1 Kings 19:4, with "LORD" and no "O", as set for the prophets. Balanced and Readable turn "my death is better than my life" into everyday words, the same in 4:8. The double quotation mark closes Jonah's prayer.

decisions.choice: "quítame la vida" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Jonah's words echo Elijah's prayer, and Spanish 1 Kings 19:4 has "quítame la vida" at every level.

decisions.choice: "uchukue uhai wangu" (L); "chukua uhai wangu" (B)
decisions.reason: The words of Elijah's prayer as the published 1 Kings 19:4 has them, which Jonah echoes.

decisions.choice: "제 목숨을 거두어 주십시오" (L, B), as Elijah's prayer in the Korean 1 Kings 19:4
decisions.reason: Jonah's request echoes Elijah's (meaning decision), so Literal and Balanced use the published words.

decisions.choice: "xin lấy mạng sống con"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision points to Elijah's prayer in 1 Kings 19:4, whose published Vietnamese has "xin lấy mạng sống con đi"; the same words are kept.

decisions.choice: toma ... a minha vida (L); tira a minha vida (B)
decisions.reason: Jonah prays Elijah's words (m1), so Literal and Balanced keep the Portuguese of 1 Kings 19:4 at their levels, "toma a minha vida" and "tira a minha vida", with "SENHOR" and no "ó", as the English has no "O".

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh, Is it doing good [that] it burns to you?

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Is it good that you are burning [with anger]?"
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Are you right to be angry?"
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Do you have a right to be angry?"

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Ngươi nổi nóng như vậy là phải sao?"
vi.B: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Con giận như vậy có đúng không?"
vi.R: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Con có quyền nổi giận như vậy sao?"

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «¿Es bueno que ardas [de ira]?».
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «¿Haces bien en enojarte así?».
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «¿Tienes derecho a estar enojado?».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Est-ce bien que tu sois brûlant [de colère] ? »
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « As-tu raison de te mettre en colère ? »
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a dit : « As-tu le droit d’être en colère ? »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Je, ni vema kwamba unawaka [hasira]?"
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Je, una haki ya kukasirika?"

ko.L: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "네가 [분노로] 달아오르는 것이 잘하는 것이냐?"
ko.B: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "네가 화를 내는 것이 옳으냐?"
ko.R: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "네가 화를 내는 것이 옳은 일이냐?"

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "É bom que tu estejas ardendo [de ira]?"
pt.B: Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Tens razão para estar irado?"
pt.R: Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Tens o direito de ficar com raiva?"

decisions.choice: is it good? Are you right to be angry?
decisions.reason: The word means "doing well", and so either "is it right" or, used as an adverb, "very" ("are you so very angry?"). Most read it as the question whether Jonah's anger is justified. It is a question, not a statement, and Jonah does not answer it until verse 9.

decisions.choice: Is it good that you are burning [with anger]? (L); Are you right to be angry? (B); Do you have a right to be angry? (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of burning anger (see 4:1). Balanced and Readable give the question in everyday words, and use the same words in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "¿Es bueno que ardas [de ira]?" (L); "¿Haces bien en enojarte así?" (B); "¿Tienes derecho a estar enojado?" (R)
decisions.reason: The question is repeated in verse 9 and answered by Jonah with the same words, so each level keeps one wording for both.

decisions.choice: "Je, unafanya vema kukasirika?" (B); "Je, una haki ya kukasirika?" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for God's question, singular "wewe" to Jonah. It is kept word for word in 4:9, where God asks again and Jonah answers with the same words.

decisions.choice: "잘하는 것이냐" (L); "옳으냐" (B); "옳은 일이냐" (R); the same words return in 4:9
decisions.reason: God's question asks whether Jonah is right to be angry (meaning decision). Each level keeps one wording so that Jonah can throw God's words back in 4:9.

decisions.choice: God says "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R) to Jonah
decisions.reason: The terms note names God's questions to Jonah in chapter 4: "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R), the address of a commission rather than a rebuke.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹנָה֙ מִן־הָעִ֔יר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב מִקֶּ֣דֶם לָעִ֑יר וַיַּעַשׂ֩ ל֨וֹ שָׁ֜ם סֻכָּ֗ה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב תַּחְתֶּ֨יהָ֙ בַּצֵּ֔ל עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִרְאֶ֔ה מַה־יִּהְיֶ֖ה בָּעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Jonah from the city and sat east of the city; and he made for himself there a booth and sat under it in the shade, until he would see what would be in the city.

en.L: And Jonah went out from the city and sat east of the city. And he made for himself a booth there and sat under it in the shade, until he could see what would happen in the city.
en.B: Jonah went out of the city and sat down to the east of it. He made himself a shelter there and sat under it in the shade, waiting to see what would become of the city.
en.R: Jonah went out of the city and sat down at a place east of it. There he made a shelter for himself and sat in its shade. He waited to see what would happen to the city.

vi.L: Giô-na ra khỏi thành và ngồi ở phía đông thành. Ông làm cho mình một cái chòi ở đó và ngồi dưới bóng nó, cho đến khi ông thấy điều gì sẽ xảy ra trong thành.
vi.B: Giô-na ra khỏi thành và ngồi ở phía đông thành. Ông dựng cho mình một cái chòi ở đó rồi ngồi dưới bóng mát, chờ xem điều gì sẽ xảy đến cho thành.
vi.R: Giô-na ra khỏi thành và ngồi ở một chỗ phía đông thành. Ở đó, ông làm cho mình một cái chòi và ngồi dưới bóng mát. Ông chờ xem điều gì sẽ xảy ra cho thành.

es.L: Y salió Jonás de la ciudad y se sentó al oriente de la ciudad; y se hizo allí una enramada y se sentó debajo de ella a la sombra, hasta ver qué sucedería en la ciudad.
es.B: Jonás salió de la ciudad y se sentó al este de ella. Allí se hizo un refugio y se sentó debajo, a la sombra, esperando a ver qué sería de la ciudad.
es.R: Jonás salió de la ciudad y se sentó en un lugar al este de ella. Allí se hizo un refugio y se sentó a su sombra. Esperaba ver qué le pasaría a la ciudad.

fr.L: Et Jonas sortit de la ville et s’assit à l’est de la ville. Et il se fit là une hutte et s’assit dessous, à l’ombre, jusqu’à ce qu’il voie ce qui arriverait dans la ville.
fr.B: Jonas sortit de la ville et s’assit à l’est de celle-ci. Il s’y fit un abri et s’assit dessous, à l’ombre, en attendant de voir ce qu’il adviendrait de la ville.
fr.R: Jonas est sorti de la ville et il s’est assis à un endroit à l’est de la ville. Là, il s’est fait un abri et il s’est assis à son ombre. Il attendait de voir ce qui allait arriver à la ville.

sw.L: Yona akatoka mjini, akaketi upande wa mashariki wa mji. Akajifanyia kibanda huko, akaketi chini yake kivulini, mpaka aone kitakachotokea mjini.
sw.B: Yona alitoka nje ya mji, akaketi upande wa mashariki wake. Akajijengea kibanda huko, akaketi chini yake kivulini, akingoja kuona yatakayoupata mji.
sw.R: Yona alitoka nje ya mji, akaketi mahali fulani upande wa mashariki wake. Huko alijijengea kibanda, akaketi kivulini mwake. Alingoja aone kitakachoupata mji.

ko.L: 그리고 요나가 그 성읍에서 나가 그 성읍 동쪽에 앉았다. 그리고 그가 거기에 자기를 위하여 초막을 만들고 그 아래 그늘에 앉아, 그 성읍에 무슨 일이 일어날지 볼 때까지 [기다렸다].
ko.B: 요나는 성읍에서 나가 성읍 동쪽에 앉았다. 그는 거기에 초막을 하나 만들고 그 아래 그늘에 앉아서, 그 성읍이 어떻게 되는지 지켜보았다.
ko.R: 요나는 성읍에서 나와 성읍 동쪽에 가서 앉았다. 그는 거기에 나뭇가지로 쉴 곳을 만들고 그 그늘에 앉았다. 그는 성읍에 무슨 일이 일어날지 기다리며 지켜보았다.

pt.L: E Jonas saiu da cidade e se sentou a leste da cidade. E fez para si ali uma cabana e se sentou debaixo dela, à sombra, até ver o que aconteceria na cidade.
pt.B: Jonas saiu da cidade e se sentou a leste dela. Fez ali um abrigo para si e se sentou debaixo dele, à sombra, esperando para ver o que seria da cidade.
pt.R: Jonas saiu da cidade e se sentou num lugar a leste dela. Ali ele fez um abrigo para si e se sentou na sombra dele. Ficou esperando para ver o que ia acontecer com a cidade.

decisions.choice: Jonah went out: what Jonah did after the LORD's question, or what he had done earlier
alternatives: Jonah had gone out, before God relented (3:10)
decisions.reason: The verse may continue the story: after the LORD's question Jonah went out to watch, still hoping that the city would be destroyed. Or it may step back to the time before 3:10, when the forty days were still running. The verb form allows both. Either way, Jonah sits and waits to see whether Nineveh will fall.

decisions.choice: a booth: a rough shelter of branches
decisions.reason: The word is used of the temporary huts of the Feast of Booths (Leviticus 23:42) and of shelters in a field (Isaiah 1:8). It gave some shade, but not enough, as the next verse shows.

decisions.choice: booth (L); shelter (B, R); what would happen in (L); what would become of (B); what would happen to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "shelter" because the reader may not know what a booth is (m2).

decisions.choice: "una enramada" (L); "un refugio" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The booth is a rough shelter of branches, which "enramada" names exactly; Balanced and Readable use a plainer word.

decisions.choice: "kibanda"
decisions.reason: A rough shelter of branches; the same Swahili word serves the English "booth" (L) and "shelter" (B, R).

decisions.choice: "초막" (L, B); "나뭇가지로 쉴 곳을 만들고" (R)
decisions.reason: A booth is a rough shelter of branches (meaning decision); "초막" is the published word for *sukkah* [Lev 23:42]. Readable says what it was.

decisions.choice: "cái chòi" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: a rough shelter of branches; "chòi" is just that, where "lều" suggests cloth or a tent.

source.text: וַיְמַ֣ן יְהוָֽה־אֱ֠לֹהִים קִיקָי֞וֹן וַיַּ֣עַל׀מֵעַ֣ל לְיוֹנָ֗ה לִֽהְי֥וֹת צֵל֙ עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ לְהַצִּ֥יל ל֖וֹ מֵרָֽעָת֑וֹ וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח יוֹנָ֛ה עַל־הַקִּֽיקָי֖וֹן שִׂמְחָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And appointed Yahweh God a qiqayon, and it went up over Jonah to be shade over his head, to deliver him from his evil; and rejoiced Jonah over the qiqayon [with] a joy great.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God appointed a plant, and it went up over Jonah to be shade over his head, to deliver him from his misery; and Jonah rejoiced over the plant [with] a great joy.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God appointed a leafy plant, and it grew up over Jonah to give shade over his head and to save him from his misery. Jonah was overjoyed about the plant.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God sent a leafy plant, and it grew up over Jonah. It gave shade to his head and eased his misery. Jonah was very happy about the plant.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời chỉ định một cây, và nó mọc lên trên Giô-na để làm bóng che trên đầu ông, để giải cứu ông khỏi sự khốn khổ của ông; và Giô-na vui mừng về cây ấy [với] một niềm vui lớn.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời chỉ định một cây lá rộng, và nó mọc lên trên Giô-na để che bóng mát trên đầu ông và cứu ông khỏi nỗi khổ sở. Giô-na vô cùng vui mừng vì cây ấy.
vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời sai một cây lá rộng mọc lên trên Giô-na. Cây ấy che bóng mát cho đầu ông và làm ông bớt khổ sở. Giô-na rất vui vì cây ấy.

es.L: Y dispuso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios una planta, y creció por encima de Jonás para ser sombra sobre su cabeza, para librarlo de su malestar; y se alegró Jonás por la planta [con] gran alegría.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios dispuso una planta, que creció por encima de Jonás para darle sombra a la cabeza y librarlo de su malestar. Jonás se alegró muchísimo por la planta.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios envió una planta frondosa, que creció por encima de Jonás. Le daba sombra a la cabeza y aliviaba su malestar. Jonás estaba muy contento con la planta.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu désigna une plante, et elle monta au-dessus de Jonas pour être une ombre sur sa tête, pour le délivrer de son mal ; et Jonas se réjouit à cause de la plante [d’]une grande joie.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu désigna une plante feuillue, qui poussa au-dessus de Jonas pour donner de l’ombre à sa tête et le délivrer de son malaise. Jonas fut tout joyeux de cette plante.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a envoyé une plante feuillue, et elle a poussé au-dessus de Jonas. Elle lui faisait de l’ombre sur la tête et le soulageait. Jonas était très content de la plante.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akaandaa mmea, ukamea juu ya Yona ili uwe kivuli juu ya kichwa chake, kumwokoa na ubaya wake; naye Yona akaufurahia mmea huo furaha kuu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akaandaa mmea wenye majani mapana, ukakua juu ya Yona ili kumpa kivuli kichwani na kumwondolea taabu yake. Yona akaufurahia sana mmea huo.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akaleta mmea wenye majani mapana, ukakua juu ya Yona. Ukampa kivuli kichwani, ukampunguzia taabu yake. Yona akaufurahia sana mmea huo.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 식물 하나를 정하여 두셔서, 그것이 요나 위로 자라 올라 그의 머리 위에 그늘이 되게 하여, 그를 그의 괴로움에서 건지게 하셨다. 요나는 그 식물 때문에 큰 기쁨으로 기뻐했다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 잎이 무성한 덩굴 하나를 마련해 두셨다. 그 덩굴이 요나 위로 자라 올라 그의 머리에 그늘을 드리워, 그를 괴로움에서 건져 주었다. 요나는 그 덩굴 때문에 몹시 기뻐했다.
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 잎이 무성한 덩굴 하나를 보내셨다. 그 덩굴이 요나 위로 자라 올라 그의 머리에 그늘을 만들어 주었다. 그래서 요나의 괴로움이 덜해졌다. 요나는 그 덩굴 때문에 아주 기뻤다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus designou uma planta, e ela subiu por cima de Jonas para ser sombra sobre a sua cabeça, para livrá-lo do seu mal; e Jonas se alegrou por causa da planta [com] grande alegria.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} Deus designou uma planta frondosa, e ela cresceu por cima de Jonas para dar sombra à sua cabeça e livrá-lo do seu desconforto. Jonas ficou muito alegre por causa da planta.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus mandou uma planta cheia de folhas, e ela cresceu por cima de Jonas. Ela fez sombra na cabeça dele e aliviou o seu sofrimento. Jonas ficou muito feliz com a planta.

decisions.choice: a plant: a fast-growing, broad-leaved plant whose kind is not known for certain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is used only in this chapter. It is often taken to be the castor-oil plant, which grows quickly and has large leaves; the Greek translation calls it a gourd. Early Christian readers debated the word: Jerome's Latin rendered it "ivy", and Augustine recorded the stir that this caused when the new rendering was read in church. The story needs only a plant that grew fast and gave shade. These descriptions of the ancient translations are written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: to deliver him from his misery: "misery" is again the book's word for evil
alternatives: to shade him from his misery
decisions.reason: The book's word for evil and disaster (see 1:2) is used here for Jonah's discomfort, and perhaps also his bad temper (4:1). The verb "deliver" sounds like the word for "shade" just before it, a play the verse makes on purpose.

decisions.choice: the LORD God: the two names together, only here in Jonah
decisions.reason: The book calls God "the LORD" and "God". Here, as God moves from Nineveh to deal with his prophet, both names stand together, as in the garden story of Genesis 2-3. The next two appointments, the worm and the wind, are by "God".

decisions.choice: Jonah rejoiced with a great joy: the only time he is glad in the book
decisions.reason: "Great" comes again (see 1:2). Jonah's great anger (4:1) becomes great joy, over a plant.

decisions.choice: appointed (L, B); sent (R); a plant (L); a leafy plant (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Appointed" keeps the same word for each thing God appoints (2:1); Readable says "sent". Balanced and Readable say "leafy" because the plant gave shade, without naming a kind (m1). Balanced says "overjoyed" for "rejoiced with a great joy".

decisions.choice: "una planta" (L, B); "una planta frondosa" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for 4:6-10; the kind of plant is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: "malestar" (all levels)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the book's word for evil; Spanish "malestar" (discomfort, misery) keeps the root "mal" heard in 4:1.

decisions.choice: "mmea" (L); "mmea wenye majani mapana" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The kind of plant is not known for certain (meaning decision), so Swahili names no species, as the English "plant" / "leafy plant".

decisions.choice: "식물" (L); "잎이 무성한 덩굴" (B, R); "{{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the kind of plant is not known (meaning decision), so Literal says only "식물" and Balanced and Readable describe it; the footnote gives the old guesses (gourd, castor-oil plant). The two names stand together, as in Genesis 2.

decisions.choice: "괴로움" for "his evil"
decisions.reason: Korean cannot say "his evil" for his misery; every level says "괴로움", and the meaning decision notes the play on the book's word.

decisions.choice: "một cây" (L); "một cây lá rộng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning footnote says the kind is not known for certain; naming a species (the older "dây dưa", or castor bean) would claim more than the text does.

decisions.choice: "une plante" (L), "une plante feuillue" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the English does not name the plant, whose kind is uncertain, so French does not say "ricin".

decisions.choice: uma planta (L); uma planta frondosa (B); uma planta cheia de folhas (R)
decisions.reason: The kind of plant is not known (m1). As the English says "a plant" and "a leafy plant" without naming a kind, Portuguese does not say "aboboreira", the gourd of older Portuguese Bibles, which comes from the Greek translation's reading, nor "rícino", the castor-oil plant many suggest; "frondosa" and "cheia de folhas" say why it gave shade.

source.text: וַיְמַ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ תּוֹלַ֔עַת בַּעֲל֥וֹת הַשַּׁ֖חַר לַֽמָּחֳרָ֑ת וַתַּ֥ךְ אֶת־הַקִּֽיקָי֖וֹן וַיִּיבָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And appointed the God a worm at the going up of the dawn on the next day, and it struck the qiqayon, and it withered.

en.L: And God appointed a worm when the dawn came up on the next day, and it struck the plant, and it withered.
en.B: But at dawn the next day God appointed a worm, which attacked the plant so that it withered.
en.R: But early the next morning God sent a worm. It chewed the plant, and the plant dried up.

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời chỉ định một con sâu khi rạng đông lên vào ngày hôm sau, và nó cắn cây, và cây khô héo.
vi.B: Nhưng rạng sáng hôm sau, Đức Chúa Trời chỉ định một con sâu cắn cây ấy, khiến nó khô héo.
vi.R: Nhưng sáng sớm hôm sau, Đức Chúa Trời sai một con sâu đến. Nó cắn cây, và cây khô héo đi.

es.L: Y dispuso Dios un gusano al subir el alba al día siguiente, y [este] hirió la planta, y se secó.
es.B: Pero al amanecer del día siguiente, Dios dispuso un gusano, que atacó la planta, de modo que se secó.
es.R: Pero temprano a la mañana siguiente, Dios envió un gusano. El gusano mordió la planta, y la planta se secó.

fr.L: Et Dieu désigna un ver, quand l’aube monta le lendemain, et il frappa la plante, et elle sécha.
fr.B: Mais le lendemain, à l’aube, Dieu désigna un ver, qui attaqua la plante, et elle sécha.
fr.R: Mais le lendemain, très tôt le matin, Dieu a envoyé un ver. Le ver a rongé la plante, et la plante a séché.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu akaandaa mdudu alfajiri ilipopambazuka siku iliyofuata, naye akaupiga mmea huo, ukanyauka.
sw.B: Lakini kesho yake alfajiri Mungu akaandaa mdudu, naye akaushambulia mmea hata ukanyauka.
sw.R: Lakini asubuhi na mapema siku iliyofuata, Mungu alimleta mdudu. Mdudu huyo akautafuna mmea, nao ukakauka.

ko.L: 그리고 다음 날 동이 틀 때에 하나님께서 벌레 한 마리를 정하여 두셨다. 그것이 그 식물을 쳐서 [식물이] 시들었다.
ko.B: 그러나 다음 날 동이 틀 무렵에 하나님께서 벌레 한 마리를 마련해 두셨다. 그 벌레가 덩굴을 갉아 먹자, 덩굴이 시들어 버렸다.
ko.R: 그러나 다음 날 이른 아침에 하나님께서 벌레 한 마리를 보내셨다. 벌레가 덩굴을 갉아 먹어서, 덩굴이 말라 버렸다.

pt.L: E Deus designou um verme quando a aurora subiu no dia seguinte, e ele feriu a planta, e ela secou.
pt.B: Mas, ao raiar do dia seguinte, Deus designou um verme, que atacou a planta, e ela secou.
pt.R: Mas, bem cedo na manhã seguinte, Deus mandou um verme. Ele roeu a planta, e a planta secou.

decisions.choice: a worm struck the plant: a small creature brings down what God gave
decisions.reason: God appoints a worm as he appointed the fish and the plant. The verb "struck" is used of the sun striking Jonah in the next verse. A grub or worm boring into the stem would kill a plant quickly.

decisions.choice: appointed (L, B); sent (R); struck (L); attacked (B); chewed (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, Literal and Balanced say "appointed", Readable "sent". Readable says what a worm does to a plant.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀כִּזְרֹ֣חַ הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ וַיְמַ֨ן אֱלֹהִ֜ים ר֤וּחַ קָדִים֙ חֲרִישִׁ֔ית וַתַּ֥ךְ הַשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ יוֹנָ֖ה וַיִּתְעַלָּ֑ף וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ֙ לָמ֔וּת וַיֹּ֕אמֶר ט֥וֹב מוֹתִ֖י מֵחַיָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it happened, as rose the sun, and appointed God a wind east scorching, and struck the sun on [the] head of Jonah, and he grew faint; and he asked his life to die, and said, Better [is] my death than my life.

en.L: And it happened, when the sun rose, that God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun struck the head of Jonah, and he grew faint; and he asked for himself that he might die, and said, "My death [is] better than my life."
en.B: When the sun came up, God appointed a scorching wind from the east, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head until he grew faint. He prayed that he might die, and he said, "Death is better for me than life."
en.R: When the sun came up, God sent a hot wind from the east. The sun beat down on Jonah's head, and he became weak and faint. He asked to die. "I would rather be dead than alive," he said.

vi.L: Khi mặt trời mọc, Đức Chúa Trời chỉ định một ngọn gió đông nóng bỏng, và mặt trời giáng xuống đầu Giô-na, và ông ngất đi; ông xin cho mình được chết, và nói: "Con chết còn hơn sống."
vi.B: Khi mặt trời mọc, Đức Chúa Trời chỉ định một ngọn gió đông nóng bỏng, và nắng chiếu gay gắt trên đầu Giô-na đến nỗi ông muốn ngất xỉu. Ông cầu xin cho mình được chết và nói: "Đối với con, chết còn hơn sống."
vi.R: Khi mặt trời mọc, Đức Chúa Trời sai một ngọn gió nóng từ phía đông thổi đến. Nắng chiếu gay gắt trên đầu Giô-na, và ông trở nên yếu ớt, choáng váng. Ông xin được chết. Ông nói: "Con thà chết còn hơn sống."

es.L: Y sucedió que, al salir el sol, dispuso Dios un viento abrasador del oriente, y el sol hirió la cabeza de Jonás, y desfalleció; y pidió para sí la muerte, y dijo: «Mejor [es] mi muerte que mi vida».
es.B: Cuando salió el sol, Dios dispuso un viento abrasador del este, y el sol le golpeaba la cabeza a Jonás hasta que desfalleció. Pidió morirse, y dijo: «Para mí es mejor la muerte que la vida».
es.R: Cuando salió el sol, Dios envió un viento caliente del este. El sol le daba de lleno en la cabeza a Jonás, y él se sintió débil y a punto de desmayarse. Pidió morirse. «Prefiero estar muerto que vivo», dijo.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand le soleil se leva, que Dieu désigna un vent d’est brûlant ; et le soleil frappa la tête de Jonas, et il défaillit ; et il demanda pour lui-même de mourir, et dit : « Ma mort [est] meilleure que ma vie. »
fr.B: Quand le soleil se leva, Dieu désigna un vent d’est brûlant, et le soleil frappa si fort la tête de Jonas qu’il défaillit. Il demanda la mort et dit : « La mort vaut mieux pour moi que la vie. »
fr.R: Quand le soleil s’est levé, Dieu a envoyé un vent chaud venu de l’est. Le soleil tapait sur la tête de Jonas, et il s’est senti faible, prêt à s’évanouir. Il a demandé à mourir. « J’aime mieux être mort que vivant », a-t-il dit.

sw.L: Ikawa jua lilipochomoza, Mungu akaandaa upepo wa mashariki wenye joto kali, nalo jua likampiga Yona kichwani, akazimia; akajiombea kufa, akasema, "Kufa kwangu [ni] bora kuliko kuishi kwangu."
sw.B: Jua lilipochomoza, Mungu akaandaa upepo wa mashariki wenye joto kali, nalo jua likampiga Yona kichwani hata akazimia. Akaomba afe, akasema, "Ni afadhali nife kuliko kuishi."
sw.R: Jua lilipochomoza, Mungu alileta upepo wa joto kutoka mashariki. Jua likawaka kwa nguvu juu ya kichwa cha Yona, akadhoofika na kukaribia kuzimia. Akaomba afe. Akasema, "Ni afadhali nife kuliko kuwa hai."

ko.L: 그리고 해가 떠오를 때에 하나님께서 뜨거운 동풍을 정하여 두셨다. 해가 요나의 머리를 내리쬐니 그가 기진하였다. 그가 죽기를 스스로 구하며 말했다. "제게는 죽는 것이 사는 것보다 낫습니다."
ko.B: 해가 뜨자 하나님께서 뜨거운 동풍을 마련해 두셨다. 해가 요나의 머리 위로 내리쬐자, 그는 기운이 다 빠졌다. 그는 죽기를 구하며 말했다. "저에게는 죽는 것이 사는 것보다 낫습니다."
ko.R: 해가 뜨자 하나님께서 동쪽에서 뜨거운 바람을 보내셨다. 해가 요나의 머리 위로 뜨겁게 내리쬐었다. 그는 힘이 빠져 쓰러질 것 같았다. 그는 죽게 해 달라고 빌었다. "저는 사느니 차라리 죽는 것이 낫겠습니다." 그가 말했다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando o sol nasceu, Deus designou um vento oriental abrasador, e o sol feriu a cabeça de Jonas, e ele desfaleceu; e pediu para si a morte, e disse: "A minha morte [é] melhor do que a minha vida."
pt.B: Quando o sol nasceu, Deus designou um vento abrasador vindo do leste, e o sol bateu na cabeça de Jonas até ele desfalecer. Ele pediu a morte e disse: "Para mim a morte é melhor do que a vida."
pt.R: Quando o sol nasceu, Deus mandou um vento quente do leste. O sol bateu forte na cabeça de Jonas, e ele ficou fraco e quase desmaiou. Ele pediu para morrer. "Prefiro estar morto a estar vivo", disse ele.

decisions.choice: a scorching east wind: the hot wind off the desert
decisions.reason: The east wind blows in from the desert, hot and dry, and withers plants (Genesis 41:6; Ezekiel 17:10; Hosea 13:15). The word for "scorching" is used only here and its sense is not certain; it may mean hot, sultry or still.

decisions.choice: he asked for himself that he might die: the words of 1 Kings 19:4
decisions.reason: The phrase is the same as Elijah's under the broom tree, as Jonah's prayer in verse 3 was. Jonah repeats his own words from verse 3, "my death is better than my life".

decisions.choice: appointed (L, B); sent (R); he asked for himself that he might die (L); he prayed that he might die (B); He asked to die (R)
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its wording of 1 Kings 19:4 for the request to die (m2) and its own wording of verse 3 for Jonah's words.

decisions.choice: "pidió para sí la muerte" (L); "Pidió morirse" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The words of Spanish 1 Kings 19:4, Elijah's request, which Jonah's echoes.

decisions.choice: "akajiombea kufa" (L); "akaomba afe" (B)
decisions.reason: The words of the published 1 Kings 19:4, which this line echoes.

decisions.choice: "죽기를 구하다" (L, B); Jonah's words in 합쇼체, as in 4:3
decisions.reason: The words of Elijah in 1 Kings 19:4 (meaning decision), where the published Korean has "죽기를 구하다". Jonah's wish is spoken to God, so it keeps the 합쇼체 of his prayer in 4:3.

decisions.choice: "xin cho mình được chết" (L); "cầu xin cho mình được chết" (B); "xin được chết" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision names 1 Kings 19:4; these are the published Vietnamese words of that verse at each level. Jonah's words are spoken to God, so he says "con", as in 4:3.

decisions.choice: um vento oriental abrasador (L); um vento abrasador vindo do leste (B); um vento quente do leste (R); pediu para si a morte (L), pediu a morte (B), pediu para morrer (R)
decisions.reason: "Vento oriental" is the term the Pentateuch's Portuguese uses for the east wind off the desert (m1); Balanced and Readable say where it came from in plainer words. The request to die keeps the Portuguese of 1 Kings 19:4 at each level (m2), and Jonah's words repeat verse 3.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־יוֹנָ֔ה הַהֵיטֵ֥ב חָרָֽה־לְךָ֖ עַל־הַקִּֽיקָי֑וֹן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֵיטֵ֥ב חָֽרָה־לִ֖י עַד־מָֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God to Jonah, Is it doing good [that] it burns to you over the qiqayon? And he said, Doing good [that] it burns to me, to death.

en.L: And God said to Jonah, "Is it good that you are burning [with anger] about the plant?" And he said, "It is good that I am burning [with anger], even to death."
en.B: But God said to Jonah, "Are you right to be angry about the plant?" "I am right to be angry," he said, "angry enough to die!"
en.R: But God said to Jonah, "Do you have a right to be angry about the plant?" "Yes, I do," Jonah answered. "I am so angry I could die!"

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời phán với Giô-na: "Ngươi nổi nóng về cây ấy như vậy là phải sao?" Ông nói: "Con nổi nóng là phải, cho đến chết."
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời phán với Giô-na: "Con giận về cây ấy như vậy có đúng không?" Ông đáp: "Con giận là đúng, giận đến muốn chết!"
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời phán với Giô-na: "Con có quyền nổi giận về cái cây ấy sao?" Giô-na đáp: "Có chứ! Con giận đến muốn chết!"

es.L: Y dijo Dios a Jonás: «¿Es bueno que ardas [de ira] por la planta?». Y él dijo: «Es bueno que arda [de ira], hasta la muerte».
es.B: Pero Dios le dijo a Jonás: «¿Haces bien en enojarte así por la planta?». «Hago bien en enojarme», respondió él, «¡tanto que quisiera morirme!».
es.R: Pero Dios le dijo a Jonás: «¿Tienes derecho a estar enojado por la planta?». «¡Sí, lo tengo!», respondió Jonás. «¡Estoy tan enojado que quisiera morirme!».

fr.L: Et Dieu dit à Jonas : « Est-ce bien que tu sois brûlant [de colère] à cause de la plante ? » Et il dit : « C’est bien que je sois brûlant [de colère], jusqu’à la mort. »
fr.B: Mais Dieu dit à Jonas : « As-tu raison de te mettre en colère à cause de la plante ? » Jonas répondit : « J’ai raison de me mettre en colère, au point d’en mourir ! »
fr.R: Mais Dieu a dit à Jonas : « As-tu le droit d’être en colère à cause de la plante ? » Jonas a répondu : « Oui, j’en ai le droit. Je suis tellement en colère que j’en mourrais ! »

sw.L: Mungu akamwambia Yona, "Je, ni vema kwamba unawaka [hasira] kwa ajili ya mmea huo?" Akasema, "Ni vema kwamba ninawaka [hasira], hata kufa."
sw.B: Lakini Mungu akamwambia Yona, "Je, unafanya vema kukasirika kwa sababu ya mmea huo?" Akajibu, "Ninafanya vema kukasirika, hata kufa!"
sw.R: Lakini Mungu akamwambia Yona, "Je, una haki ya kukasirika kwa sababu ya mmea huo?" Yona akajibu, "Ndiyo, ninayo! Nimekasirika kiasi kwamba ningependa kufa!"

ko.L: 그러자 하나님께서 요나에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 그 식물 때문에 [분노로] 달아오르는 것이 잘하는 것이냐?" 그가 말했다. "제가 죽기까지 [분노로] 달아오르는 것이 잘하는 것입니다."

pt.B: Mas Deus disse a Jonas: "Tens razão para estar irado por causa da planta?" "Tenho razão para estar irado", disse ele, "irado a ponto de morrer!"
pt.R: Mas Deus disse a Jonas: "Tens o direito de ficar com raiva por causa da planta?" "Tenho, sim", respondeu Jonas. "Estou com tanta raiva que eu poderia morrer!"

decisions.choice: Jonah answers the question of verse 4 with God's own words
decisions.reason: God asks again, now about the plant, and Jonah throws the words back: "it is good" that he is angry. "To death" means as angry as a person can be, angry enough to wish to die (Judges 16:16; Matthew 26:38).

decisions.choice: the same wording as verse 4 for the question, at each level
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of verse 4, so that the reader can hear the question repeated. Readable makes Jonah's answer a plain "Yes".

decisions.choice: God's question keeps the wording of 4:4, and Jonah answers with the same words ("là phải" L; "là đúng" B)

decisions.choice: you had pity: you felt for it, you would have spared it
decisions.reason: The verb means to look with pity on something and to spare it (Ezekiel 20:17; Joel 2:17). The same verb is God's in verse 11. The argument moves from the lesser to the greater: if Jonah grieves over a plant, how much more should God care for a city.

decisions.choice: the son of a night: what grew up in one night
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, "son of" can describe something by what belongs to it: "a son of a night" is something that lasts a night. The plant came up in a night and was gone in a night.

decisions.choice: had pity (L); took pity (B); cared about (R); [as] the son of a night (L); in a night (B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the same verb here and in verse 11 (m1). Literal keeps the idiom "the son of a night"; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m2). Readable joins "you did not labor" and "you did not make it grow" into one phrase.

decisions.choice: "tuviste lástima" (L); "tuviste compasión" (B); "Te preocupaste" (R), and the same verb for God in verse 11
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb for Jonah's feeling for the plant and God's for Nineveh; each level keeps one Spanish verb for both.

decisions.choice: "[como] hija de una noche" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "son of a night", in the feminine to agree with "planta".

decisions.choice: "아끼다" (L); "아까워하다" (B, R) in 4:10, and the same verb for God in 4:11
decisions.reason: The verb is pity that would spare something (meaning decision); Korean "아끼다 / 아까워하다" says both feeling for it and wishing to keep it, and the same verb in God's question in 4:11 keeps the book's closing comparison.

decisions.choice: "[như] con của một đêm"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom, bracketed as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable give its sense, "in one night".

decisions.choice: "[comme] fille d'une nuit"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom is "son of a night"; French "plante" is feminine, so the idiom is put in the feminine to agree with it.

fr.B: Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, ne devrais-je pas avoir pitié de Ninive, cette grande ville, où il y a plus de 120 000 personnes qui ne savent pas distinguer leur main droite de leur main gauche, et des animaux en grand nombre ? »

pt.L: E eu, não terei pena de Nínive, a grande cidade, em que há mais de cento e vinte mil seres humanos que não sabem [distinguir] entre a sua mão direita e a sua esquerda, e muitos animais?"

pt.R: Então eu não deveria me importar com a grande cidade de Nínive? Mais de cento e vinte mil pessoas moram lá, e elas não sabem distinguir a mão direita da esquerda. E há também muitos animais."

decisions.choice: who do not know their right hand from their left: who are helpless, without understanding
alternatives: people without the knowledge of God's law
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe the whole population as morally helpless, lacking the understanding God gives, or it may count the city's small children, too young to tell right from left. The text does not explain it. Either way, they are people in need of mercy, not judgment.

decisions.choice: more than 120,000: twelve times ten thousand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "more than twelve ten-thousands". The number shows how many lives were at stake, whether it counts all the city's people or only its children (m1).

decisions.choice: should I not have pity? The book ends with God's question
decisions.reason: The LORD asks Jonah, and the reader, whether he should not care for a great city full of people, and even its animals. The book does not give Jonah's answer. It closes on God's compassion for a foreign and enemy city, the very thing Jonah confessed in 4:2.

decisions.choice: have pity (L); take pity (B); care about (R); human beings (L); people (B, R); 120,000 (all levels)
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as in verse 10 at each level. The number is written in figures, as numbers over ninety-nine are. Readable states the facts about the city in sentences of their own after the question. The double quotation mark closes the LORD's words and the book.

decisions.choice: "120 000" (all levels)
decisions.reason: Spanish writes numbers of four or more digits with a space.

decisions.choice: "120,000" in figures
decisions.reason: Numbers of a hundred and more are written in figures with a comma, as the published Isaiah 37:36 (185,000) and the term sheet; smaller numbers in running text are words.

decisions.choice: "120,000명" in figures at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet's number rule: large numbers are in figures in Korean at every level.

decisions.choice: "thương tiếc" (L), as for the plant in 4:10; "thương xót" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the same verb for Jonah's feeling for the plant and God's for Nineveh; Literal keeps one word for both. For a city of living people Balanced and Readable say "thương xót", since "tiếc" is said of what is already lost.

decisions.choice: "hơn 120.000 người", in figures
decisions.reason: Numbers of 100 and above are written in figures with a thousands dot, as the terms note asks; "vạn" would echo the Hebrew "myriads" but is now rare.

decisions.choice: "avoir pitié" (L, B), "s'inquiéter pour" (R), the same verb as 4:10 at each level
decisions.reason: God's question picks up Jonah's pity for the plant, so each level repeats its word from verse 10.

decisions.choice: cento e vinte mil; não sabem distinguir a mão direita da esquerda
decisions.reason: Portuguese writes a round number like this in words in running text (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 5), where the English uses figures. Balanced and Readable say "não sabem distinguir a mão direita da esquerda", the plain Portuguese for the idiom (m1); Literal brackets "distinguir" and keeps "entre".
